content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read_document on candidate_specs.md and any trigger hardware/rate or simulation guidance documents. Extract the three allowed algorithm names, deployability constraints, allowed threshold range, and any stated allocated Level-1 trigger rate requirement."},{"id":"s2","description":"From candidate_specs.md, identify which of the three candidate algorithms are deployable in the Level-1 trigger hardware. Exclude any non-deployable candidate from optimization, and record numeric deployability flags if needed: 1 for deployable, 0 for not deployable."},{"id":"s3","description":"Run simulate_efficiency for each deployable candidate algorithm at a coarse grid of thresholds: 20, 30, 40, 50, and 60 GeV. Record each returned signal efficiency as a numeric result associated with its algorithm and threshold."},{"id":"s4","description":"For the candidate/threshold region with the highest coarse-grid efficiency, run simulate_efficiency at a finer threshold spacing within the allowed 20-60 GeV range, focusing around the best coarse threshold and including nearby integer or 5 GeV thresholds as appropriate. Record all returned efficiencies numerically."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare all simulated deployable algorithm/threshold points and identify the combination with the highest signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate. Record the winning algorithm identifier, threshold in GeV, and efficiency numerically for the reporting module to use in the final recommendation."}]}
